correctness.rationale: Generating both orientations on each three-element support gives 40 permutations. Their distinct ordered subwords form a regular CW complex with simplex face posets and f-vector (6,30,120,247,194,40). Reconstructing the oriented face incidences and applying a separate topological sort verifies the 311 disjoint reversed Hasse edges are acyclic, with critical counts one vertex, six 3-cells and eight 4-cells. Independently computing integer Smith forms of the unreduced boundaries (including checking their composition) gives ranks (5,25,95,146,40) and Betti numbers (1,0,0,6,8,0). Thus the critical 4-to-3 differential has rank zero over Q, hence is zero over Z; this confirms the needed conclusion without relying on the uploaded signed recurrence. In that Morse CW model the 3-skeleton is a wedge of six S³, and the Hurewicz isomorphism makes each vanishing cellular boundary equivalent to a null attaching map. Purity is dimension five, so nonzero lower-degree homology obstructs pure shellability.
residual_risks: The proof text could explicitly add that a 3-cell paired downwards contributes zero in the signed reduction, as the frozen checker does. The independent Betti and acyclicity calculation bypasses that convention. The result is only for the complete six-letter three-cycle class.

value.rationale: Using the whole three-cycle class selects a natural generator family, rather than arbitrary permutations. The result gives a pure five-dimensional example with lower homology in two different degrees and an actual two-connected integral wedge type. It distinguishes homology, homotopy and shellability for a specific natural complex beyond the general low-connectivity bounds and Euler-characteristic data.
residual_risks: No claim of first occurrence over alphabet sizes, a general family formula, or equivariant classification.
